author: Marshall; Hargreaves
name_in_asr: Sravasti; Jetavana; old city, home of Kasyapa; Kanishka's stupa
asr_identification: Jetavana = Saheth, Sravasti = Maheth (Gonda/Bahraich), E gate of the Jetavana where Cunningham put it; Kāśyapa's town possibly near Bhitti village, 2.5 miles W(N) of Maheth; Kanishka stupa = Shah-ji-ki-Dheri (Peshawar)
evidence: Jetavana: Kushana Bodhisattva inscribed as set up 'in the Jetavana of Sravasti'; early-Kushana concrete road to the E gate, Kushana coins in monasteries F and G; temple 2 = Gandhakuti, temple 3 = Kosambakuti. Bhitti: small early town site, 56-ft square brick stupa to its N (bricks of Mauryan size). Shah-ji-ki-Dheri (Hargreaves): cruciform base 180 ft, little stupa by the E steps, monastery wall facing the stupa
quote: it is possible that the ancient town in question is to he located on a site near tlie village of Bhitti, about two and a half miles in a direction slightly nortli of west from the western ramparts of Maheth … set up this Bodhisattva statue in the Jetavana of ^ravasti … it is now amply evident that General Oimningham was right in his location of the east gate.
note: Śrāvastī/Jetavana agree with Mizutani and Cunningham (asr) and are confirmed by inscription. Kāśyapa's birthplace (06.01.14): Marshall's Bhitti suggestion holds only if Beal's '16 li' is right (he prefers the 60 li of Julien, Watters, Legge); Cunningham's Tandwa (asr) not discussed; Mizutani gives no site. Hargreaves' Shah-ji-ki-Dheri work compares the plan with Xuanzang's account (frescoes, two small stupas by the E steps) and confirms Mizutani's 02.04.03.

author: Hirananda Sastri
asr_identification: Kasia (Gorakhpur district): the stupa behind the Nirvana temple = the parinirvana caitya; Ramabhar stupa, nearly a mile SW of Kasia, = Cunningham's cremation site
evidence: shaft in the Nirvana Stupa: copper vessel covered by a copper-plate deposited in the 'Nirvana-chaitya' by Haribala (donor of the Nirvana statue), with coins of Kumaragupta; small earlier stupa inside; clay sealings 'Mahaparinirvana bhikshu-sangha' (c. 4th c.) in building Q; Ramabhar: Mauryan-brick circular stupa, drum 112 ft, shaft to water level, no relics
quote: At the end of the document it is recorded that the plate was deposited in the Nirvdna-chaitya ” and that Haribala was the donor … the legend (1. 1) Mahd'pa/pini/i'vdiia (1. 2) hhilcsMi-sangha … Bamabhar is the name of the locality which Cunningham identified with Makutahandhana, the spot where the remains of Buddha were cremated.
note: Inscription and sealings support Mizutani's Kuśinagara = Kasia and nirvāṇa site (06.04, 06.04.03) and Cunningham's (asr, ASR 01). Ramabhar dug as a very old stupa but nothing decides the cremation site (06.04.11): Mizutani puts the present cremation site c. 10 miles E and doubts it; the survey's Ramabhar Tila is restated, not proved.

author: Pargiter
asr_identification: Kasia = Kuśinagara: the large stupa behind the Nirvana temple
evidence: copper-plate (Nidana-sutra, ink) deposited by Haribala, dated by coins of Kumaragupta (d. 455) to the 3rd quarter of the 5th c.
quote: The stupa, in which this plate was deposited, is the large stupa behind the Nirvdna temple, and is named in the inscription the Nir'odna-cTiaitya certainly and the ’Farinirvayia-chaitya probably … this plate virtually testifies that tradition had declared even earlier than that, that Buddha died at fTasia and that Kasia is Ku^inagara.
note: Confirms Mizutani's Kasia and Cunningham's identification (asr) by inscription: the name was attached to the spot by the mid-5th c. — the tradition, not proof of the historical site.

author: Stein
asr_identification: no Xuanzang site at Sahri-Bahlol or Takht-i-Bahi (Yusufzai, Peshawar district)
evidence: excavation of six mounds shows most shrines abandoned and ruined long before the 7th c.; none of Xuanzang's traceable Gandhara routes passed Sahri-Bahlol
quote: If the shrines of Sahii-Bahlol and Takht-i-Bahi are not among the fifteen specifically mentioned by him … we can only conclude that worship at them had ceased … None of Hsuan-tsang’s traceable routes in Gandhara took the pilgrims past Sahri-Bahlol
note: Against Cunningham's Sahri-Bahlol = Ekaśṛṅga town with Takht-i-Bahi as the 'high mountain' (asr 02.04.16, ASR 05 p. 42); see 236 for Stein's site. Mizutani gives no site for 02.04.16.

evidence: site traced on the ground (following Deane); a mutilated Sahri-Bahlol relief read as Ekasringa carrying the courtesan (Hargreaves doubts the reading, not the site)
quote: Hsiian-tsang relates it in connection with a convent which he places about a hundred U to the north-west of Po-lu-sha or Shahbaz-garhi and ‘ to the south of a great mountain.’ … at the site of ‘ Butan ’ near the southern foot of the Shahkot Pass and above the large village of Palai in Swat territory.
note: Moves Cunningham's Sahri-Bahlol (asr) to Butan; Mizutani gives no site. Assumes Po-lu-sha = Shahbaz Garhi (Mizutani 02.04.14 agrees; Cunningham: Palodheri).; 02.04.14 removed (Stein only measures from Shahbaz Garhi)

But it very soon became apparent
note: Rejects Cunningham's Babar-khana head-gift stupa (asr 03.03.04); Mizutani's Bhallar stupa is Marshall's later view. Taxila (03.03) agrees with Mizutani and Cunningham. Kumrahar: Spooner overturns Waddell's single Asoka pillar, which Mizutani follows for 08.02.05; the survey's Panch-Pahari pillar (asr) is not discussed.
